member_targets: The physiological mechanism by which abrupt transfer from sheltered indoor conditions to full outdoor sunlight, wind, and temperature swings injures or stresses unacclimated seedlings.
The outcomes or damage seedlings suffer when moved directly from indoor conditions to full outdoor exposure without gradual acclimation
The physiological mechanism by which incremental exposure to outdoor conditions enables seedlings to adjust successfully, as contrasted with the reason abrupt transfer fails

An identification of which particular outdoor environmental conditions (e.g., specific combinations of light intensity, wind, and temperature) impose the greatest physiological stress on seedlings during the hardening-off period, ranking or specifying the most stressful conditions rather than describing the hardening-off schedule itself.
The typical duration (number of days) of the hardening-off period before seedlings are transplanted outdoors permanently.
The typical duration (number of days) of the hardening-off period for indoor-started seedlings.
The duration (number of days, or length of the gradual exposure period) that hardening off should last before seedlings are planted outside permanently.
The typical duration, in number of days, of the hardening-off period for most seedlings.
